title: Infinitesimal points are the mixed points
statement: For any scheme S and group scheme G over S [def-sc-group-scheme], let infPoints(G) be its S[η]-points reducing to the identity, and let mixedPoints(G) be its S[ε][δ]-points reducing to the identity on each axis, using [def-sc-dual-numbers]. The map induced by η↦εδ is a bijection infPoints(G)→mixedPoints(G).

source.place: Chapter 10, infinitesimal points; coefficient-extraction argument in Bracket.lean toMixed_bijective docstring

proof.text: Injectivity: equality after η↦εδ gives equality of the underlying continuous maps and of the section maps after applying DualNumber.mulRingHom. Transport sections along the equality of preimage opens. Extracting fst twice recovers the original constant coefficient and extracting snd twice recovers the original infinitesimal coefficient. Extensionality gives equality of the original scheme morphisms and infinitesimal points.

For a mixed point z, use the mixed-coefficient derivation theorem. Its reduced point g is the identity section by either axis restriction. Construct v from this specified derivation using pointOfDerivation, whose existing theorems make v a morphism over S reducing to the identity.

To check v maps to z, compare all four coefficients of every section map. The constant coefficient agrees by the definition of g, both pure coefficients vanish by the two axis restrictions, and the mixed coefficient agrees by the defining formula for D. Scheme and subtype extensionality finish surjectivity.
